content: Palisades Medical Center is a regional healthcare facility located in North Bergen, New Jersey. The hospital is equipped with approximately 202 inpatient beds and provides medical services to an estimated population of 350,000 residents in Southern Bergen and Hudson counties. Since 1999, Palisades Medical Center has been a member of the NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital network and maintains an academic affiliation with the Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons. Previously known as North Hudson Hospital, the facility was originally situated in Weehawken, New Jersey. In 1978, the hospital was relocated to the waterfront area of North Bergen and subsequently renamed Palisades Medical Center. On September 21, 2007, actor George Clooney and an accompanying individual were admitted to Palisades Medical Center for medical care following a motorcycle accident. Prior to any official statement from the hospital, information regarding Clooney's status as a patient was leaked to the media, raising concerns about a potential internal breach of confidentiality. Following an internal audit, it was revealed that 27 hospital employees had accessed Clooney's medical records without proper authorization. As a result, all 27 employees were suspended from their positions for a duration of one month without pay. The individuals involved included nurses, support staff, and security personnel; however, no physicians were implicated in the breach. A labor union representing some of the affected staff members has contested seven of the suspensions.
